name: cache-clock
description: Status-line countdown to prompt-cache expiry; keeps small contexts warm and compacts large ones before the cache lapses

ttl.title: Prompt-cache TTL
ttl.description: The cache lifetime to count down from. auto: Claude Code's own settings and environment (promptCacheTtl, the TTL variables, Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry), then the cache's behaviour (two misses within the hour = 5m); 1h until either is known. Set 5m on an API key to skip the two misses

autoAct.title: Act before the cache lapses
autoAct.description: Off: countdown and a warning toast only

leadMinutes.title: Minutes before expiry to act (1-hour TTL)
leadMinutes.description: When to ping or compact on a 1-hour cache (study 2026-10-07: 0.5-5 minutes within 1 point; 3 leaves margin for a slow request)

leadMinutes5m.title: Minutes before expiry to act (5-minute TTL)
leadMinutes5m.description: When to ping or compact on a 5-minute cache: 0.5 acts at 4:30 of quiet. Acting at 2:30 pinged or compacted for people who were about to come back (study 2026-10-08: 43% vs 24% of idle-gap cost). Raise it if /cache-clock shows missed pings

keepAliveBelowTokens.title: Keep warm with pings below this context size
keepAliveBelowTokens.description: Below this, ping up to the keep-alive limit and then let the cache lapse

maxKeepAlives.title: Keep-alive pings per idle stretch (small contexts)
maxKeepAlives.description: Each ping buys one more TTL of warmth

compactAboveTokens.title: Compact at the first deadline above this context size
compactAboveTokens.description: Between the keep-alive limit and this, ping once and compact at the second deadline
